reason: Reject. The kernel's precomputed reciprocal division (MULTIPLIER = ceil(2^34/7) = 2454267027, SHIFT = 34, residual 5) is not exact across the full uint32 domain that problem.txt — the operative contract here, since no test.py/get_inputs exist — explicitly requires ("EVERY unsigned 32-bit value is legal, from 0 through 4294967295 inclusive... Every coordinate must equal the integer mathematical target EXACTLY"). Confirmed runtime probes (t8, t9) on legal, in-domain values show: (c1) for large values ≡ 6 mod 7 (3435973841, 4294967284, 4294967291), the kernel row equals floor(v/7)+1, mismatching the exact int64 reference; (c2) for failing values (3435973841, 4294967291) the stored col wraps in unsigned arithmetic to 4294967295, outside the contract-mandated [0,6], and 7·row+col != original index, violating the contract's explicit recomposition invariant. Both claims are in_scope with scope evidence citing the stated input domain. No contract clause accounts for this deviation — the contract permits any division method only "if it satisfies this exact requirement for every legal unsigned index." Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence and found no new claims; no open claims remain. This is a genuine correctness defect, not a metric artifact or tolerance issue.
